newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rain impact on Australia cotton unclear - ACF.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rain impact on Australia cotton unclear - ACF.

text.p: A full assessment of potential rain and flood damage to Australia's 1996/97 cotton crop would not be known until about March 1, Claire Braund, communications manager for the Australian Cotton Foundation, said on Monday.
Braund was speaking after conducting a preliminary assessment of potential damage after the weekend of further heavy rain in northern New South Wales.
"All that we know definitely is that it (the crop) will not be above 2.5 million (500-pound bales)," she told Reuters.
This is the still-current forecast of the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE).
As earlier reported, a consensus of industry and trade sources contacted by Reuters on Monday was that the crop was likely to be reduced to 2.4 million bales by the wet weather.
Some growers said that if brilliant weather emerged there could be an increase in yields. But if rain persisted, grades would be the major issue, Braund said.
Rainfall had been very variable, with nine inches reported over the weekend by one farm in Moree in northwestern New South Wales and only two inches recorded at a farm 60 km away, she said.
Other issues such as whether farms were on rivers or behind levees also created a variable impact which was still under assessment, she said.
"There will be some impact but what it is we don't know," she said.
Picking could be delayed by flooding, but the extent of delays also depended on the weather, she said.
Picking of Australia's northernmost cotton crop, at Emerald in southeast Queensland, is due to begin in four to eight weeks.
